h: וַיֵּלֶךְ וְשַׁבָּת תְּשׁוּבָה, ד׳ Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah, 4
"Is It Not Because My God Is Not in My Midst?": Teshuvah in Thought and the Hiding of the Face

p: "And he will say on that day:
הֲלֹא עַל כִּי אֵין אֱלֹהַי בְּקִרְבִּי
'Is it not because my God is not in my midst
that these evils have befallen me?'
And I will surely hide My face
עַל כָּל הָרָעָה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וְגוֹ׳"
for all the evil that he has done, etc."
The Ramban, z"l, raised a question on this:
of the hiding of the Face come
"Is it not because my God is not in my midst
that they have befallen me, etc."?
For surely this is teshuvah and regret,
since he has accepted the judgment upon himself as just.
that here it is teshuvah by thought of the heart alone;
עַל כֵּן הוּא עֲדַיִין בְּהֶסְתֵּר פָּנִים,
therefore he is still under the hiding of the Face,
But when he returns with confession,
about this it says in Parashas Nitzavim,
"And you will return unto, etc.," "and He will return, etc."
surely the saying of Chazal is well known
on condition that 'I am a tzaddik,'
even if he is a complete rasha,
for perhaps he thought of teshuvah in his heart."
We see, then, that even if we now see
from his deeds that he is a complete rasha,
the most severe sins, such as idolatry
if at that moment he thought of teshuvah,
he would be considered a complete tzaddik.
and through this the redemption came about.
that even a thought of teshuvah alone
is effective only if it is
"until He Who knows all secrets testifies about him
that he will never return to that sin" —
And about this it is said,
that is, as soon as he returns
before He Who knows all secrets, etc. —
"for you have stumbled in your iniquity":
immediately it is considered as unintentional.
And this is the allusion in this parashah:
"And he will say on that day,
עַל כִּי אֵין אֱלֹהַי בְּקִרְבִּי מְצָאוּנִי" –
'Because my God is not in my midst they have befallen me'" —
that is, that he will have a thought of teshuvah
then, "And I will surely hide My face
for all the evil that he has done" —
the sin will be hidden and erased
even for all the evils in the world,
even "for he turned to other gods."
However, in order that the sin be rectified completely,
so that it be counted as merits,
about this it is said in Parashas Nitzavim,
"And you will return unto Hashem your God
and listen to His voice, etc.":
גַּם אִם יִהְיֶה נִדַּחֲךָ בִּקְצֵה הַשָּׁמַיִם,
even if your dispersed are at the end of the heavens,
and "from there" specifically "He will take you" —
He will gather you and take you.
This is in the manner of what they said in the Gemara
on the pasuk "and through them he shall live"
and he receives reward for them.
So too, the gathering and the taking
will come about specifically through the sins,
for through his teshuvah they will become like merits.
And this is when the teshuvah is
meaning that through this he draws closer
to Hashem Yisbarach all the more,
in the greatness of his teshuvah.
And as it is stated in the Pesikta
Great is the power of teshuvah,
for as soon as a person thinks in his heart
and not merely to the first firmament, etc.,
And in the Gemara as well it is stated
for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory,
That is, by the power of his teshuvah,
even if with his sins he reached
up to the Throne of Glory,
that they have no share in Olam Haba,
such as one who denies the fundamental principle,
as is known, that "Imma nests in the Throne,"
which is the Throne of Glory,
the aspect of Binah, the World to Come.
וְגַם כֵּן אִיתָא בִּפְסִיקְתָּא זוֹ שָׁם
And it is also stated in this Pesikta there,
'For my iniquities have gone over my head'"
'For our iniquities have multiplied above our head, etc.'"
That is, that it reaches up to the root,
and this is heresy, may the Merciful One save us.
when one is sunk very deeply in them
with all his senses and powers,
as it is stated regarding Rabbi Elazar ben Durdaya
as it is said, 'All who come to her do not return,
nor do they attain the paths of life'"
and nevertheless it was said about him,
"There is one who acquires his world in a single hour,"
for he merited that they be transformed into merits,
as it is said, "And when a rasha returns, etc.,
And it says further in the Pesikta, earlier on:
לְבֶן מֶלֶךְ שֶׁהָיָה רָחוֹק מֵאָבִיו וְכוּלֵּי;
to a prince who was far from his father, etc.;
His father sent word and said to him,
הֲלֹךְ מַה שֶּׁאַתָּה יָכוֹל לְפִי כֹּחֲךָ,
'Go as far as you can, according to your strength,
and I will come to you for the rest of the way.'
'Return to Me and I will return to you'"
That is: even if a person has distanced himself
through his drawing a little closer from his side,
as it is said, "with Me is the crushed one."
across which it is not in a person's power to return,
as it is said, "I am with the crushed one, etc."

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 49b — "On condition that I am righteous — even if he is completely wicked, she is betrothed, for perhaps he thought thoughts of teshuvah in his mind. On condition that I am wicked — even if he is completely righteous, she is betrothed, for perhaps he thought of idolatry in his mind."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Va'eschanan 12 — “It is in the Pesikta (Shuvah): Rabbeinu HaKadosh expounded, Great is the power of teshuvah, for as soon as a person thinks in his heart to do teshuvah, it immediately rises for him up to… and stands before the Throne of Glory.” Connection: Both hold that a thought of teshuvah in the heart already takes effect at once.

paragraphs.text: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 2:2 — "And what is teshuvah? That the sinner abandon his sin, remove it from his thoughts and resolve in his heart never to do it again, as it says, 'Let the wicked abandon his way' (Yeshayahu 55:7); and also regret the past…; and He Who knows hidden things will testify about him that he will never return to this sin."

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86b — "Reish Lakish said: Great is teshuvah, for deliberate sins become for him like unintentional ones, as it says, 'Return, Israel, to Hashem your God, for you have stumbled in your iniquity' (Hoshea 14:2)… But Reish Lakish said: Great is teshuvah, for deliberate sins become for him like merits, as it says, 'And when the wicked turns from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness, on account of them he shall live' (Yechezkel 33:19)! There is no difficulty: here, from love; there, from fear."

paragraphs.text: Pesikta Rabbasi 44 — "Rabbeinu HaKadosh expounded: Great is the power of teshuvah, for as soon as a person thinks in his heart to do teshuvah, immediately it rises — not ten mil, not twenty, not a hundred, but a journey of five hundred years; and not to the first firmament but to the seventh; and not only to the seventh, but it stands before the Throne of Glory. So Hoshea says, 'Return, Israel, unto (ad) Hashem your God' (Hoshea 14:2)."

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86a; Tzidkas HaTzadik 40; Takanas HaShavin 10:3 — transformed sin and the remaining process of atonement: Yoma distinguishes forgiveness through teshuvah from the completion of kapparah: depending on the transgression, Yom Kippur, suffering, or death may still complete the cleansing. Tzidkas HaTzadik explains the highest teshuvah as an illumination in which deliberate sins can be understood as merits within Divine knowledge, while the earlier discussion in this siman nevertheless retains worldly punishment for grave acts. Rav Tzadok is therefore distinguishing two planes: the act’s inner meaning and covenantal root may be transformed, while its visible damage in this world may still require purification. The Gemara states the stages of atonement; this root-versus-appearance formulation is Rav Tzadok’s synthesis.

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 17a — Of Elazar ben Durdaya: "He said: The matter depends only on me. He placed his head between his knees and wept aloud until his soul departed. A heavenly voice went forth and said: Rabbi Elazar ben Durdaya is destined for the life of the World to Come." The Gemara applies to him "'All who come to her do not return, nor attain the paths of life' (Mishlei 2:19)," for since he was so deeply attached to that sin, it is like heresy.
